section_summary: This section chiefly documents State Department, Commerce Department, Army, and SCAP processing of applications for business and official travel to occupied Japan, Korea, and Okinawa during July–August 1948. It includes commercial-applicant lists, military-clearance notices, passport instructions, diplomatic representations for individual travelers, and cases involving repatriation or onward migration. Several tangentially filed documents concern Soviet personnel in Japan and tourism in Guatemala.

subfiles.title: Yokohama despatch A-155 on tourist-party passport applications
subfiles.about: Reports passport agencies' uncertainty about procedures for organized tourist travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Pan American Airways reported that New York and San Francisco passport agencies lacked instructions for processing Japan tour participants.

subfiles.title: Singapore telegram 148 concerning Mrs. de Villiers
subfiles.about: Requests forwarding of Mrs. de Villiers's entry clearance to Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Singapore asks that Mrs. de Villiers's clearance be sent to the American consul in Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department transmittal of approved applicants
subfiles.to: Herbert Corkran Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits applicants approved for Japan and Korea travel, subject to SCAP approval.
subfiles.summary: Commerce forwards its approved applicant list and copies of foreign applicants' forms.

subfiles.title: Applicants approved by Commerce for Japan and Korea travel
subfiles.about: Lists commercial representatives, firms, nationalities, locations, requested entry dates, and travel methods.
subfiles.summary: The list covers applicants associated with Boston, Cleveland, Detroit, Honolulu, Los Angeles, New York, and San Francisco firms. It records citizenship, current location, proposed entry periods, transport, and occasional Korea requests.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Tehran authorizing previous documentation procedure
subfiles.about: Authorizes use of an earlier procedure when necessary to enable an unnamed traveler.
subfiles.summary: The Department permits Tehran to use the previously authorized travel-documentation procedure if necessary.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Mrs. de Villiers's application
subfiles.about: Records SCAP's request for details justifying Mrs. de Villiers's business travel.
subfiles.summary: Rawls requested her company name, Japanese business, and reasons her presence was necessary, warning approval would require at least two weeks.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting business details from Mrs. de Villiers
subfiles.to: American Consul, Shanghai, for Mrs. George V. de Villiers
subfiles.about: Requests additional information required by SCAP for her Japan application.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. de Villiers is asked to identify her company, its Japanese business, and why her presence is necessary.

subfiles.title: Receipt for Bernard Jacob Etzin's military permit
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Etzin's August 1948 return permit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Shackleford acknowledges military permit 7738, valid for Etzin's return journey to Japan during August 1948.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Etzin's reentry documentation
subfiles.about: Records arrangements for Etzin's eventual reentry into the United States.
subfiles.summary: Etzin's Japan permit required onward or U.S. reentry authorization; Immigration promised to mail his reentry permit that day.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on the Guide for Commercial Entrants to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports distribution and shipment of additional copies of the commercial-entrants guide.
subfiles.summary: Seventy-five additional guides were sent to the Department, while copies went to numerous Foreign Service posts and the Army.

subfiles.title: South African note transmitting Burt Nieburg's application
subfiles.from: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Transmits and endorses Burt Nieburg's application for entry to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The South African Legation submits Nieburg's sponsored business-travel application and requests notification of the result.

subfiles.title: Burt Nieburg business-visit application
subfiles.about: Applies to visit Tokyo, Kobe, and Nagoya to purchase woolen raw materials.
subfiles.summary: Nieburg proposes a one-to-two-week buying trip by air as a director of South African clothing manufacturer Greys Ltd.

subfiles.title: Referral of Nieburg application to the Army
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of Burt Nieburg's application.
subfiles.summary: Protective Services forwards the South African-sponsored application and asks the Military Permit Section to report SCAP's decision.

subfiles.title: Notification of Nieburg's approved Japan entry
subfiles.to: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Notifies the Legation of Nieburg's clearance and passport-notation requirements.
subfiles.summary: Nieburg may enter between October 15 and November 15 for fifteen days. The note explains that his passport must contain the clearance statement prescribed by SCAP Circular 3.

subfiles.title: Dalian despatch on repatriation of Najiy and Anisa Kurbangali
subfiles.about: Seeks help obtaining passports and family contact for two Japan-born sisters blocked from leaving Dalian.
subfiles.summary: Although SCAP authorized Najiy and Anisa Kurbangali to enter Japan, Soviet authorities refused their departure for lack of passports. Paddock forwards photographs and a family letter to Tokyo, requests confirmation of the family's address, and supplies a Shanghai return address.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Munir Safra's proposed travel
subfiles.about: Explains that Safra must first apply through the Commerce Department.
subfiles.summary: Corkran directed attorney Harry Grossman to Frank J. Nolan's Commerce office to begin Safra's Japan application.

subfiles.title: Harry Grossman letter concerning Munir Safra
subfiles.about: Requests expedited Japanese entry arrangements for Barclay Metal Corporation agent Munir Safra.
subfiles.summary: Grossman reports that Safra, a Turkish-passport holder in Hong Kong, wants the American Consulate notified promptly.

subfiles.title: Blank records search slip
subfiles.about: Blank form for recording searches, cross-references, and previous attachments.
subfiles.summary: Unused records-search form with fields for references, remarks, search date, and clerk's initials.

subfiles.title: Richard Krautheimer letter about Paul Ehrlich
subfiles.about: Inquires about his South African brother Paul Ehrlich's Japan visa application.
subfiles.summary: Krautheimer asks the Department to advise on or expedite Paul Ehrlich's visitor application before Ehrlich continues his journey.

subfiles.title: Military clearance memorandum for Paul Ernst Ehrlich
subfiles.about: Grants Ehrlich a sixty-day Japan clearance with an August–September entry window.
subfiles.summary: Ehrlich may enter Japan between August 10 and September 10 and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Reply to Richard Krautheimer concerning Ehrlich
subfiles.about: Confirms that SCAP approved Paul Ehrlich's travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Chappell states that the South African Legation was notified of Ehrlich's August 10–September 10 entry authorization.

subfiles.title: FAO letter supporting Adrian Acock's travel
subfiles.from: G. E. Overington, Food and Agriculture Organization
subfiles.about: Requests permits for Adrian Acock's official mission to Japan and South Korea.
subfiles.summary: FAO supports Acock's participation in a joint UN working party on agricultural production requisites in the Far East.

subfiles.title: Adrian Acock application for occupied-territory travel
subfiles.about: Applies for a two-week official visit to Tokyo and South Korea.
subfiles.summary: The Australian scientist describes his residence and travel history and identifies the UN agricultural working party as his mission. The reverse contains standard occupied-territory instructions and certifications.

subfiles.title: Referral of Acock application to the Army
subfiles.about: Forwards Acock's application and supporting information for military consideration.
subfiles.summary: Chappell explains Acock's FAO mission, notes Rawls's informal agreement to handle the case, and requests a decision.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Acock's departure
subfiles.about: Records that Acock would await Japan clearance in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Patricia Albers reported Acock's August 2 departure; Corkran promised to notify the Shanghai consulate after clearance.

subfiles.title: Telegram concerning Victor Moche's delayed journey
subfiles.about: Reports a travel delay affecting Victor Moche's Japan entry permit.
subfiles.summary: The poorly preserved telegram advises that Moche's onward travel was unavoidably delayed.

subfiles.title: South African note concerning Morio S. Yoshii
subfiles.from: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Transmits Yoshii's application to return permanently to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Legation states that Yoshii had lived in South Africa since 1932 and had no adverse record.

subfiles.title: Morio Sakari Yoshii return application
subfiles.about: Applies to return by ship to his family in Hiroshima Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Yoshii seeks permanent return and plans to travel on an emergency certificate issued in Pretoria.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Yoshii's permanent return
subfiles.to: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Explains that Japanese nationals need no advance permission to return permanently.
subfiles.summary: The Department advises that Yoshii is free to travel to Japan without special documentation.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Jakob Szpiro's clearance
subfiles.about: Notifies Irwin Spiro of Jakob Szpiro's approved Japan entry.
subfiles.summary: Mellor reported Szpiro's sixty-day clearance and planned a company-funded notification telegram to Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Military clearance memorandum for Jakob Szpiro
subfiles.about: Confirms Szpiro's authorization to enter Japan during August.
subfiles.summary: Szpiro received sixty-day clearance for entry between August 1 and 31, with two passport photographs required.

subfiles.title: Letter confirming Jakob Szpiro's clearance
subfiles.about: Confirms SCAP approval and notification of Szpiro in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Chappell confirms Szpiro's August entry window, sixty-day stay, and the telegram sent to the Shanghai consulate.

subfiles.title: File memorandum extending Victor Moche's entry period
subfiles.about: Records Army consent to extend Moche's Japan entry authorization through August.
subfiles.summary: During an Army visit, Corkran obtained Rawls's consent to extend Moche's entry period.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Singapore extending Moche's authorization
subfiles.about: Extends Victor C. Moche's permissible entry period through August.
subfiles.summary: Singapore may furnish Moche a certified telegram copy or amend his documentation.

subfiles.title: Blank document charge sheet
subfiles.about: Blank form for recording a document's date, security class, recipient, and charging office.
subfiles.summary: Unused Department of State document charge form.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Jakob Szpiro in Shanghai
subfiles.about: Provides Szpiro's clearance terms and substitute documentation instructions.
subfiles.summary: Szpiro may enter during August for sixty days and use a certified telegram copy in lieu of the required passport statement.

subfiles.title: Commerce transmittal of July 30 applicant list
subfiles.to: Herbert Corkran Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits another list of applicants approved for Japan travel.
subfiles.summary: Commerce forwards its approved Japan applicants, subject to final SCAP action.

subfiles.title: Applicants approved by Commerce for travel to Japan
subfiles.about: Lists applicants from several U.S. cities, their firms, nationalities, locations, dates, and transportation.
subfiles.summary: The list covers numerous Japanese, U.S., Chinese, European, and other commercial representatives. It records requested entry periods, logistics needs, previous approvals, and a permit-extension request.

subfiles.title: English translation of Argentine Embassy note 535
subfiles.about: Requests assistance for four Japanese residents authorized to immigrate to Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Argentina asks U.S. authorities in Japan to help Kameyada and Shinki Tokashiki, Seiki Ohshiro, and Yoshiko Ohshiro depart.

subfiles.title: Spanish original of Argentine Embassy note 535
subfiles.about: Spanish-language request for assistance to Japanese emigrants bound for Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The original note identifies the emigrants' Okinawan addresses and Argentine landing-permit numbers.

subfiles.title: Tehran telegram 915 concerning Afzharieh
subfiles.about: Reports Afzharieh's request for an October entry period using the earlier procedure.
subfiles.summary: Tehran relays Afzharieh's requested October 1–31 Japan entry dates.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Tehran on Iranian travel documentation
subfiles.about: Limits substitute documentation and requires new applications for changed clearance dates.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks why Iran cannot annotate passports and says Afshar, Ghandehari, and Afzharieh need new applications unless earlier dates remain usable.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Moise Shammah's clearance
subfiles.about: Notifies Whitehill Associates that Shammah received Japan clearance.
subfiles.summary: Evelyn Masser confirmed Shammah was in Shanghai and agreed that Whitehill Associates would pay the notification cable.

subfiles.title: Military clearance memorandum for Moise Shammah
subfiles.about: Grants Shammah sixty-day clearance for entry during August 1948.
subfiles.summary: The clearance identifies Shammah in Hong Kong as Whitehill Associates' representative and requires two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Moise Shammah in Shanghai
subfiles.about: Provides Shammah's clearance terms and substitute documentation.
subfiles.summary: Shammah may enter Japan during August for sixty days and receive a certified telegram copy instead of a passport notation.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Maurice de Botton in Alexandria
subfiles.about: Provides de Botton's clearance terms and documentation instructions.
subfiles.summary: De Botton may enter Japan August 5–September 5 for sixty days and use a certified telegram copy.

subfiles.title: Military clearance memorandum for Maurice de Botton
subfiles.about: Confirms de Botton's sixty-day clearance and entry window.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum identifies de Botton as Mediterranean Merchants Company's representative in Alexandria.

subfiles.title: Maurice de Botton commercial-travel application
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks permission for de Botton to purchase Japanese tobacco in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The firm describes de Botton as its Portuguese assistant treasurer and explains plans to purchase about one million pounds of tobacco. It records the company's business, banking, prewar Tokyo agent, itinerary, and requested sixty-day stay.

subfiles.title: Commerce transmittal of August 6 applicant list
subfiles.to: Herbert Corkran Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits approved applicants for Japan and Korea travel.
subfiles.summary: Commerce forwards its latest approved applicant list and foreign applicants' forms for final SCAP action.

subfiles.title: Applicants approved by Commerce for Japan and Korea
subfiles.about: Lists commercial representatives and requested travel from numerous U.S. locations.
subfiles.summary: The list records applicants' firms, citizenship, present location, proposed dates, transport, and logistics requirements. Most seek Japan entry; the final entry requests Korea travel for Robert H. Rinear.

subfiles.title: Nanking telegram supporting Edward Carter's Tokyo visit
subfiles.about: Urges approval of Edward Carter's proposed Institute of Pacific Relations visit to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Stuart argues that Carter's regional scholarly tour and SCAP's reeducation program make refusal undesirable.

subfiles.title: Reply to Ambassador Stuart on Edward Carter
subfiles.about: Confidentially reports that military authorities are considering Carter's permit.
subfiles.summary: The Department advises Stuart that Carter's Japan request remains under military review.

subfiles.title: Guatemala despatch 397 on United Fruit tourism promotion
subfiles.from: Milton K. Wells, U.S. Embassy, Guatemala
subfiles.about: Reports an editorial praising United Fruit Company's promotion of tourism to Guatemala.
subfiles.summary: El Imparcial rebutted allegations against foreign transport companies by citing United Fruit publicity and passenger statistics. Wells suggests the controversy relates to efforts to restore funding for Guatemala's National Tourist Office.

subfiles.title: Shanghai telegram on Mrs. de Villiers's imminent arrival
subfiles.about: Urges action before Mrs. de Villiers reaches Japan without clearance.
subfiles.summary: The telegram supplies her professional role, joint ownership of Globe Potteries, South African sponsorship, itinerary, and prior application history. Shanghai warns that refusing her landing would have unfortunate repercussions.

subfiles.title: Turkish Embassy note requesting commercial entry
subfiles.about: Requests Japan entry for Ektas Türk Limited's director, then waiting in Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: The Turkish Embassy seeks commercial-entry permission for its applicant in Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: Reply requesting details of Zeki Keribar's trade
subfiles.about: Reports that military authorities need details of goods Keribar intends to buy and sell.
subfiles.summary: The Department recounts its referral of Zeki Keribar's request to the Army. Theater Headquarters requires the specific goods involved before considering his application further.

subfiles.title: Referral of Zeki Keribar request to the Army
subfiles.about: Asks the Army to submit Keribar's commercial-entry request to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Chappell identifies Keribar as Ektas Türk Limited's director in Hong Kong and requests notification of SCAP's decision.

subfiles.title: Czechoslovak memorandum supplying information on Joseph Zuna
subfiles.about: Details Zuna's transport and intended machinery sales and textile and shellac purchases.
subfiles.summary: Zuna would fly by Pan American, sell four kinds of Czechoslovak machinery, and buy Japanese textiles and shellac.

subfiles.title: Referral of supplemental Zuna information
subfiles.about: Forwards the Czechoslovak Embassy's additional information for SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: Chappell transmits Zuna's itinerary and proposed trade and requests a memorandum if clearance is granted.

subfiles.title: Notification of Joseph Zuna's clearance
subfiles.about: Confirms Zuna's approval and explains the required passport notation.
subfiles.summary: Zuna may enter Japan between September 1 and October 1 and remain sixty days. The Department encloses the commercial-entrants guide and cites SCAP Circular 3 for the required passport statement.

subfiles.title: Army action slip for Joseph Zuna
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Records Zuna's sixty-day clearance and September–October entry window.
subfiles.summary: Army action slip granting Joseph Zuna clearance for sixty days.

subfiles.title: Duplicate action slip recording Zuna's entry dates
subfiles.about: Records authorization for entry between September 1 and October 1, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate action slip noting Zuna's authorized entry period.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on Soviet personnel in Japan
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Soviet entry and exit activity and the current Soviet mission's strength.
subfiles.summary: Exit requests by Soviet families were roughly balanced by new entries. As of July 26, the Soviet presence totaled 261 staff, dependents, tribunal members, and prosecution-section personnel.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Thomas Ellis Carr's Okinawa clearance
subfiles.about: Provides Carr's Okinawa clearance and arrival-reporting instructions.
subfiles.summary: Carr may enter Okinawa August 10–September 10, must report to G-2 at Naha, and carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on misrouting Thomas Ellis Carr's permit
subfiles.about: Records correction of the Army's accidental routing of Carr's permit to the Passport Division.
subfiles.summary: Rawls acknowledged the error; Simpson urgently forwarded the permit, while Mellor prepared the Hong Kong telegram amid inquiries from Bogatko.
